emily: Heads-up — saw a 95th->99th tail jump on micro-lane merges this morning, looks correlated with the merge-bridge hitting headroom. :thinking:

raj: Ooh. Which tenant/job? Any logs or quick repro?

emily: tenant=tensor-svc, observed ~07:12 UTC. Repro in staging when small & long seqs mix. Trimmed log below.

emily: ```
[07:12:01] merge-bridge: window_opened lane_id=42 capacity=128
[07:12:01] enqueue: req=abc seq_len=8
[07:12:02] enqueue: req=def seq_len=256
[07:12:02] packer: blocked waiting for headroom
[07:12:03] flush small batch due to deadline
[07:12:04] latency(req=abc)=420ms
```

kevin: That pattern screams headroom fragmentation — small reqs wait while bigs take slots, then deadline forces send -> tail.

raj: Could we tweak preemptive-fill to let small fast-paths go when bigs are present? Or soft-reserve N slots for tiny bins?

emily: Past soft-reserve experiments helped smalls but starved mediums. Thinking of heuristics: detect heterogenous seq distribution and bias coalesce window toward small sequences when smalls exceed X%.

kevin: How expensive to sample distribution? We already maintain a little seq_hist per-lane for quantization hints.

emily: Cheap — reuse seq_hist[0..4] counters. Sketch of rule:

emily: ```json
{"if_small_pct > 0.6": "micro_window_ms = 8; allow_up_to = 3 small-only batches per_epoch"}
```

raj: Two concerns: 1) precise metric & SLO triggers, 2) fairness vs throughput. Favoring smalls will increase bigs' latency.

sre-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026-314 - tail-latency spike - tagging owners @runtime

kevin: Idea: token-aware scoring for packer ordering. score = request.tokens / expected_service_time; order by score but cap starvation via max_wait_ms.

emily: Score-based ordering is appealing. Risk: ordering state complexity and replay on preemption. Could be implemented locally inside merge-bridge to limit blast radius.

raj: Combine both: score for ordering, plus a "fast-path edge" that bypasses coalesce for very small requests (<16 tokens) when headroom low. That keeps tiny interactions snappy.

emily: Agreed. Plan: canary in staging — implement small-fast-path + score-ordering behind two feature flags. Spike today, run 24h, compare p50/p95/p99 for small/medium/large.

kevin: :thumbsup:

raj: Also add metrics: fast_path_utilization, deferrals_due_to_bigs, score_reorders_count. Need dashboards before canary.

emily: Will add metrics and a dashboard. Opening PR and linking here.

emily: PR: https://git.company/re/runtime/merge-bridge/compare/fast-path

kevin: Leave flags off in prod until we validate. We'll gate rollout with canary policy.

emily: Yep — flag default = off, canary = staging -> small subset prod. If regress, rollback via flag.

emily: Thanks — will post results and updated graphs tomorrow.
